newsitem.title: BELARUS: Police beat, arrest Belarus demonstrators.
newsitem.headline: Police beat, arrest Belarus demonstrators.

text.p: Police beat demonstrators protesting against hardline Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko on Friday as they cleared an unauthorised rally in the centre of the capital, Minsk.

A Reuters correspondent on Independence Square in the city centre saw police arrest dozens of people -- including several journalists. Some of those arrested looked dazed but there was no sign of bloodshed. Police forced them to the ground and used truncheons on them before bundling them into lorries and cars.
About 1,000 mostly young activists had gathered on the square at 5 p.m. (1500 GMT) to start a tour of Western embassies in the capital to register their opposition to Lukashenko's authoritarian rule.
Authorities had sanctioned the gathering but banned people from marching through the streets. When the protesters started leaving the square, police moved in to stop them.
About 200 police with truncheons were waiting around the square. Others waited in sidestreets. They shouted orders over loudspeakers to clear the area several times before moving in.

Minsk authorities have also banned protesters from marching through the capital on Saturday, when opposition forces plan a big rally to mark Constitution Day. Police arrested a senior opposition figure overnight in what opposition officials described as an attempt to scare people away from the protest.
